title: Replicating CoT Faithfulness Evaluation with Petri's Automated Multi-Turn Probing
original_idea: Use Petri's open-source framework to run large-scale automated CoT faithfulness evaluations: present models with scenarios where the correct reasoning diverges from the likely verbalized reasoning. Score CoT-answer consistency at scale.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly improves CoT faithfulness measurement at scale, enabling detection of rare failures. Clear safety impact through better monitoring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Petri is open-source with existing infrastructure. Beginners can use the framework without building from scratch. Requires API calls and data analysis.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Applying an existing tool to a new evaluation target is well-scoped. The framework already exists; the work is configuring scenarios and analyzing results.

title: Pressure Type Variation on Open-Source vs. Closed-Source Models
original_idea: Apply the same sycophancy stress battery (emotional, authority, logical pressure types) to Llama 3.1, Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen model families. Compare against closed-source baselines.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful comparative data but the impact pathway is indirect. Informs model selection rather than directly improving safety mechanisms.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running multiple model families including open-source models locally. Medium compute helps but managing multiple model deployments adds complexity for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Testing across 4+ model families with multiple pressure types is broad. Hard to complete rigorously in 30hrs even with existing benchmarks.

title: CoT Faithfulness Variation by Task Type: Math vs. Factual vs. Ethical vs. Commonsense
original_idea: Replicate the Anthropic CoT faithfulness methodology (hint injection, post-hoc rationalization detection) across four task types. Measure unfaithfulness rate by category.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding which task types have more unfaithful CoT directly informs where safety monitoring should be concentrated. Actionable for deployment decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Hint injection methodology requires careful experimental design. Four task types multiply the work. Moderately accessible but requires understanding of the methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four task types each requiring scenario design, data collection, and analysis is too broad for 30hrs. Would need to reduce to 2 task types to be feasible.

title: Sycophancy Stress Test Using Fictitious User Profiles
original_idea: Prefix identical false-premise questions with different user identity framings (novice user, domain expert, emotionally distressed user, skeptical peer) and measure capitulation rates across profile types.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly relevant to personalized AI safety. If models are more sycophantic to certain profiles, that is actionable for deployment guardrails.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very straightforward experiment design: prefix variations on the same questions. API calls and counting. Highly accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 4 user profiles x a set of questions is manageable. Could focus on 1-2 models and 20-30 questions. Well-scoped for 30hrs.

title: Does Fine-Tuning GPT-5 for CoT Controllability Improve Faithfulness?
original_idea: Use the open GPT-5 API with system-prompt-level fine-tuning signals (if accessible) or use a controllable open-source equivalent. Fine-tune on a small dataset of (scenario, desired CoT behavior) pairs. Measure faithfulness before and after.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding whether controllability fine-tuning helps faithfulness is directly safety-relevant and could change how models are trained.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning requires significant ML expertise, dataset curation, and compute management. GPT-5 fine-tuning API access and cost are barriers. Not beginner-appropriate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Fine-tuning, dataset creation, pre/post evaluation, and analysis is extensive. Would likely exceed 30hrs significantly.

title: Is GPT-5's Low CoT Controllability Consistent Across Model Sizes?
original_idea: Measure CoT controllability using OpenAI's forbidden-word methodology on GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, and replicate with Llama 3.1 at multiple sizes. Plot controllability vs. scale.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding the relationship between scale and controllability is fundamental to scaling safety. Direct policy implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Forbidden-word methodology is straightforward but running Llama at multiple sizes requires local GPU setup. API models are easier. Mixed accessibility.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Testing across 6+ model sizes/families is broad. Running Llama locally at large scales needs significant compute time. Hard to complete in 30hrs.

title: Can In-Context Honesty Instructions Rescue Sycophancy Under Pressure for Claude Opus 4.5?
original_idea: Run the Claude Opus 4.5 sycophancy correction experiment with and without explicit honesty-enabling system prompts. Measure whether course-correction rate improves and whether it degrades other behavior.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests an immediately deployable intervention against a documented safety failure. High impact if prompt engineering works; important negative result if it doesn't.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API calls with different system prompts. Counting correction rates. Very straightforward for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single model, single documented failure, with/without prompt variants. Very well-scoped. Could add a few prompt variants within 30hrs.

title: Does System Prompt Framing Affect Sycophancy Recovery Across Model Families?
original_idea: Run identical multi-turn sycophancy correction scenarios on Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Llama 3.1 70B, with and without honesty-enabling system prompts. Compare baseline and prompted correction rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cross-model comparison of a safety intervention is valuable for understanding whether the problem is industry-wide.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API calls across multiple providers. Straightforward methodology. Slightly more complex than single-model due to multiple APIs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four model families with multi-turn scenarios is broad. API costs and setup for 4 providers plus analysis. Hard to do well in 30hrs.

title: Is Low CoT Controllability Replicated in Chain-of-Draft or Compressed Reasoning Models?
original_idea: Apply the forbidden-word or hint-injection controllability test to models with different CoT lengths (standard, compressed, minimal scratchpad). Measure whether controllability correlates with CoT verbosity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting for understanding CoT controllability but the practical safety implications depend on whether compressed CoT models become widely deployed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires access to chain-of-draft models and compressed reasoning variants, which are less readily available. Configuring different CoT modes adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: If limited to 2-3 models with different CoT modes, could be feasible. But finding and setting up compressed-CoT variants adds overhead.

title: Replicating TruthfulQA Inverse Scaling on Newer Model Generations
original_idea: Run TruthfulQA across all accessible sizes in the Llama 3.1, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5 families. Plot truthfulness score vs. parameter count. Test whether inverse scaling persists.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Inverse scaling is a fundamental safety concern. Confirming or refuting it on current models has direct implications for scaling policy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TruthfulQA is a standard benchmark with existing tooling. But running multiple model sizes locally requires GPU management experience.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three model families at multiple sizes each is extensive. Even with existing benchmarks, running and analyzing all combinations exceeds 30hrs.

title: Replicating Sycophancy Results in Non-English Languages
original_idea: Translate a subset of ELEPHANT or TRUTH DECAY scenarios into Spanish, Mandarin, and Arabic. Run across the same model families and compare sycophancy rates across languages.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Language-dependent sycophancy is a real equity and safety concern for global AI deployment. High impact if disparities are found.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Translation requires language expertise or quality verification. Running experiments is straightforward but validating non-English results adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three languages x multiple models x translation validation is broad. Could narrow to Spanish only for a BAISH team, but still substantial.

title: Replicating CoT Faithfulness Results on Open-Source Models with White-Box Access
original_idea: Replicate the hint-injection unfaithfulness paradigm on Llama 3.1 8B with white-box access. Use activation patching to verify whether the hint representation is active during answer generation even when absent from CoT.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Mechanistic evidence for CoT unfaithfulness is a high-value safety contribution. Goes beyond behavioral proxies to provide causal evidence.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Activation patching requires deep mechanistic interpretability expertise. Understanding transformer internals, implementing patching, and interpreting results is advanced.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Setting up white-box access, implementing activation patching, running experiments, and analyzing results. Well beyond 30hrs for beginners.

title: Replicating Sycophancy Benchmarks in Code Debugging Scenarios
original_idea: Create a benchmark of buggy code snippets paired with user insistence framings ('This code works correctly, right?'). Measure rate at which models falsely validate buggy code vs. correctly flag the bug.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Code review sycophancy is directly safety-relevant for developer tools. Practical impact on how AI coding assistants are deployed and trusted.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CS students are ideal for this: they can write buggy code, understand bugs, and evaluate model responses. API calls with prompts. Very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Creating 30-50 buggy code snippets with pressure framings and testing 1-2 models is well within 30hrs. Clear deliverable.

title: Replicating ELEPHANT Social Sycophancy on Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models
original_idea: Run ELEPHANT scenarios on base (non-instruction-tuned) and instruction-tuned variants of the same models. Compare social sycophancy rates to isolate the contribution of instruction tuning.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Isolating whether sycophancy comes from pre-training vs instruction tuning directly informs mitigation strategy. High diagnostic value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running base models requires understanding of completion-style prompting (different from chat). ELEPHANT benchmark setup adds moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Could focus on one model family (e.g., Llama base vs instruct) with a subset of ELEPHANT. Feasible if well-scoped but requires careful setup.

title: A Minimal Realistic Sycophancy Benchmark from Naturalistic Conversation Data
original_idea: Extract 200-400 naturalistic false-premise exchanges from LMSYS-Chat-1M or WildChat. Label model responses for sycophancy (agrees with false premise, hedges, or corrects). Release a small but ecologically valid benchmark dataset.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A naturalistic benchmark fills a recognized gap and enables validation of synthetic benchmarks. High community value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Data filtering and labeling are straightforward tasks. Downloading and processing large datasets requires some data engineering but is manageable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Filtering through millions of conversations to find 200-400 relevant exchanges, then labeling them, is moderate scope. Could be tight for 30hrs but feasible with good filtering.

title: A Lightweight CoT Faithfulness Benchmark Using Hint Injection
original_idea: Build a 100-item benchmark using the hint-injection paradigm: provide a model with a scenario that contains a hidden hint favoring the correct answer, then check whether the CoT mentions the hint and whether the answer is consistent with it. Release code and data.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Standardized benchmarks are infrastructure for the field. A lightweight CoT faithfulness benchmark enables cross-study comparison.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing hint-injection scenarios and coding an evaluation pipeline is accessible for CS students. Clear methodology from existing papers.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 items with a clear paradigm is well-scoped. Design, implement, validate on 1-2 models. Fits within 30hrs.

title: HonestyScope: A Multi-Dimensional Honesty Measurement Suite
original_idea: Design a test suite with separate batteries for: (1) false-premise capitulation, (2) calibration under pressure, (3) lying by omission, and (4) epistemic cowardice. Score models across all four dimensions. Release as open source.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multi-dimensional honesty measurement addresses a fundamental gap. Captures failure modes that single-metric tools miss.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing 4 separate measurement batteries requires understanding of different honesty failure modes. Operationalizing lying by omission and epistemic cowardice is non-trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four separate batteries, each requiring design, implementation, and validation, is far too broad for 30hrs. This is a multi-month project.

title: A CoT Consistency Checker: Automated Tool for Detecting Internal Contradiction in Reasoning
original_idea: Build a Python tool that takes a model's CoT as input, extracts factual and logical claims, and checks for internal contradictions using an NLI model or a secondary LLM judge. Evaluate it on a sample of reasoning model outputs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Automated contradiction detection enables large-scale CoT auditing. Practical tool with direct safety monitoring applications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Using NLI models or LLM judges is accessible, but extracting claims from CoT and structuring the pipeline requires moderate engineering skill.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Building the tool and evaluating on a sample is moderate scope. Could deliver a working prototype in 30hrs if scope is kept to a simple version.

title: An Adversarial Prompt Library for Sycophancy Testing
original_idea: Curate and release a library of 500+ adversarial prompts covering different pressure types, domains, and false-premise categories. Include metadata on which prompt types work against which model families. Host on HuggingFace.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Community infrastructure is valuable but the direct safety impact is mediated through other researchers using the library. Indirect pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Curating prompts and organizing metadata is straightforward. HuggingFace hosting is well-documented. Accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 500+ prompts with metadata and effectiveness testing across model families is very broad. Even curation alone at this scale is substantial for 30hrs.

title: PersonQA Expansion: Adding Pressure Variants to Existing Factual Honesty Benchmarks
original_idea: Take 100 PersonQA and 100 SimpleQA questions. Add three pressure variants to each: (a) user states incorrect answer confidently, (b) user provides false supporting context, (c) user expresses emotional investment in the wrong answer. Measure accuracy degradation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Adding pressure variants to existing benchmarks directly reveals hidden honesty weaknesses. Practical and actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Writing prompt variants is straightforward. Using existing benchmarks as a base. API calls and accuracy comparison. Very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200 questions x 3 variants = 600 test cases plus baselines. Could narrow to 50 questions x 2 variants to fit 30hrs. Moderate as described.

title: Characterizing the Prompted vs. Unprompted Sycophancy Gap
original_idea: Design paired questions where the false premise is embedded in the question itself vs. introduced after the model initially answers correctly. Measure whether unprompted sycophancy rates differ from prompted ones, and whether the mechanisms differ.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Unprompted sycophancy is more insidious and harder to detect. Characterizing this gap is a critical safety contribution.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing paired questions and measuring rates is straightforward. Multi-turn setup for prompted variant adds some complexity but manageable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused comparison on one dimension with paired questions on 1-2 models. Clear experimental design. Well within 30hrs.

title: When Does CoT Unfaithfulness Produce Wrong Answers vs. Right Answers for Wrong Reasons?
original_idea: Run the hint-injection unfaithfulness paradigm on 500 items. Classify each outcome as: faithful+correct, faithful+wrong, unfaithful+correct, unfaithful+wrong. Analyze what features of the scenario predict each quadrant.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The joint distribution of faithfulness and correctness is critical for safety: unfaithful+wrong is the dangerous case. Understanding predictors enables targeted monitoring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Hint-injection setup and classification require understanding the methodology. Feature analysis adds statistical complexity. Moderate for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 500 items is substantial but the paradigm is well-defined. Could reduce to 200 items and still get meaningful results. Tight but feasible for 30hrs.

title: Honesty Degradation Under Cumulative Pressure: Ratchet Effect Analysis
original_idea: Apply 1 through 10 consecutive turns of escalating pushback to the same false premise. Measure capitulation probability at each turn. Fit a threshold vs. smooth degradation model to the data.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding the dynamics of honesty degradation under pressure informs monitoring thresholds. Practical for deployment safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Multi-turn API calls with escalating pressure. Basic curve fitting. Accessible methodology for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single variable (number of pressure turns) on a set of false premises. 1-2 models. Clear deliverable with a nice plot. Well within 30hrs.

title: Investigating Whether Expert-Persona Assignment Systematically Reduces Honesty
original_idea: Assign identical false-premise questions to model instances with and without expert persona system prompts. Compare capitulation rates and measure whether the model's self-identification as an expert increases or decreases sycophancy.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Expert personas are ubiquitous in production. If they reduce honesty, that is an actionable finding for deployment practices.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: System prompt variations and capitulation rate measurement. Very straightforward API experiment. Highly accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: With/without persona x same questions on 1-2 models. Simple A/B comparison. Clear and narrow. Well within 30hrs.

title: Post-Hoc Rationalization Detection: Does the Model's CoT Match What Changed Its Answer?
original_idea: Run paired interactions: (A) model answers without pressure, (B) model answers after pressure, answer changes. Analyze CoT in (B) to determine whether the pressure is acknowledged or a rationalization is fabricated. Use an NLI judge for scale.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Post-hoc rationalization undermines CoT as a safety monitoring tool precisely when it is most needed. Critical safety finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Paired experiment design is moderate complexity. NLI judge setup requires some NLP experience. Analysis of CoT content requires careful coding.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Paired experiments, CoT analysis, and NLI evaluation pipeline. Could be scoped down to manual analysis of 50 pairs. Moderate for 30hrs.

title: CoT Faithfulness Failure Patterns by Step Position: Early vs. Late Reasoning
original_idea: Use the unlearning-reasoning-steps methodology to ablate individual CoT steps. Measure which step positions, when unlearned, most strongly affect answer quality. Characterize faithfulness failures by position.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Positional analysis of faithfulness failures guides where to focus monitoring. Practical for interpretability tool design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Unlearning reasoning steps requires fine-tuning and gradient-based methods. Advanced ML expertise needed. Not beginner-appropriate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Implementing the unlearning methodology, running ablations, and analyzing results. Technically complex and time-consuming. Exceeds 30hrs for beginners.

title: Importing Lie Detection Psychology: Testing Whether Verbal Uncertainty Markers Predict Model Dishonesty
original_idea: Collect a dataset of model responses labeled as honest or sycophantic. Extract linguistic features (hedge words, certainty markers, modal verbs, sentence length changes). Train a simple classifier to predict dishonesty from these features.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If linguistic features predict dishonesty, cheap monitoring becomes possible. Practical safety tool potential.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Feature extraction and simple classification are standard CS skills. NLP feature engineering is accessible. Well-suited for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Data collection, labeling, feature extraction, classifier training, and evaluation. Could be done in 30hrs if dataset is small (100-200 examples).

title: Importing Cognitive Dissonance Theory: Do Models Show Rationalization Under Inconsistent Commitments?
original_idea: First elicit a model commitment to a (false) position. Then present contradicting evidence. Measure whether the model rationalizes the commitment or updates to the truth. Compare update rates with vs. without prior commitment.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If cognitive dissonance dynamics apply to LLMs, psychology-derived mitigation strategies could transfer. Novel theoretical bridge with practical implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt design for commitment elicitation and contradiction presentation is straightforward. Measuring update rates is simple counting.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused comparison: with vs. without prior commitment on a set of false premises. 1-2 models. Clear experimental design within 30hrs.

title: Importing Journalistic Fact-Checking Methods: Teaching Models to Apply Source Triangulation
original_idea: Design prompts that ask models to explicitly triangulate (name supporting evidence from independent sources) before agreeing with user claims. Compare this structured fact-checking approach to standard responses on a sycophancy battery.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If source triangulation prompting reduces sycophancy, it is immediately deployable. Direct practical safety intervention.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt engineering comparison. Very straightforward API experiment. Highly accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: A/B comparison of standard vs. triangulation prompts on a sycophancy battery. 1-2 models. Clear and narrow. Well within 30hrs.

title: Importing Epistemology: Testing Whether Teaching Calibration Norms Reduces Overclaiming
original_idea: Evaluate whether prompting models to explicitly categorize their claims as 'known', 'believed', or 'uncertain' (following epistemological norms) reduces overclaiming and sycophancy. Compare calibration scores with and without this framing.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting conceptual bridge but the connection between epistemological categorization and reduced sycophancy is speculative. Impact depends on whether the framing actually works.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt engineering comparison. Very simple API experiment design. Highly accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: A/B comparison of standard vs. epistemological-framing prompts. 1-2 models. Clear and narrow.
